title: Abhinavagupta's crystal argument already addresses Buddhist self-awareness theory
central_reading: The crystal argument (without vimarśa, consciousness is insentient like a crystal) applies to any account that treats self-awareness as derivative — including the Buddhist svasaṃvitti phala-model. If self-awareness is a result of cognition, it can be absent when cognition is absent; but consciousness cannot be absent from itself.

claims.text: Abhinavagupta's crystal argument — that without vimarśa consciousness would be insentient like a crystal — applies to any account where self-awareness is derivative rather than intrinsic. The Buddhist phala-model makes self-awareness a result of cognition: if cognition produces self-awareness, then before cognition there is no self-awareness, leaving consciousness insentient. The crystal argument refutes this by showing that consciousness cannot be insentient at any moment, therefore self-awareness must be intrinsic (svabhāva), not produced (phala).
claims.quote: Without vimarśa, consciousness would be insentient, like a crystal
claims.hetu: if self-awareness is produced by cognition, then before cognition there is no self-awareness
claims.sadhya: the crystal argument refutes any derivative account of self-awareness, including svasaṃvitti phala-model
claims.vyapti: If consciousness cannot be insentient at any moment, self-awareness must be intrinsic, not produced.
claims.falsifier: Show that the Buddhist phala-model does not imply periods without self-awareness — i.e., that cognition is continuous and self-awareness is co-extensive with it, making the result-as-nature distinction merely verbal.

targets.rationale: Extends crystal argument to explicitly cover the Buddhist phala-model.
If crystal argument refutes the phala-model, the Buddhist response needs a different account of self-awareness.
Narrows the crux: the question becomes whether any derivative account of self-awareness is coherent.
